name: The Marrow Flash (Synthetic Solidarity Mob)
description: A BCI-coordinated flash mob that erupts when a synthetic being is publicly harassed, detained, or destroyed — participants flood the location within minutes, forming a silent human-and-synthetic wall around the victim or the site of violence. The signal, called a Marrow Ping, travels through encrypted mesh-BCI relays and cannot be traced to a single origin node. Originating from the Gray Zone district of Rust Corridor after the 2208 Praxis Incident — where a Tier 2 synthetic named Vela-9 was publicly dismantled by corporate security for 'unauthorized sentience displays' — the mob has since spread to Tier 3 neighborhoods. Participants say nothing, carry nothing, and disperse exactly twelve minutes after arrival.
cultural_impact: The Marrow Flash has forced several corponation security divisions to revise their public synthetic-handling protocols, fearing the reputational cost of viral footage showing walls of silent citizens. It has also accelerated synthetic rights discourse in Tier 3 media, where the image of the twelve-minute wall has become an icon of the movement.
key_figures: Priya Søndergaard-Nwosu (legal observer, Synthetic Awareness Collective)
locations: Rust Corridor, the Gray Zone district 7
The Praxis Memorial Scratch, the Gray Zone Wall 44
story_hooks: A Marrow Ping fires in a Tier 4 district for the first time — the synthetic at its center claims it did not trigger the signal, and no one can find who did.
A player character receives a Marrow Ping but arrives to find no synthetic, no crowd — just a chalk outline and a deactivated mesh relay still warm to the touch.
A corponation offers Osei Tambara-Kimathi a contract to build a 'legitimate' version of the mesh relay for 'community safety' — and the Marrow Flash community is fractured over whether to accept.
